problem: Embodied navigation is evaluated almost entirely in simulation, but it is unknown whether simulator rankings of methods hold on real robots; simulator artifacts such as wall-sliding let learned agents cheat, so sim results may not transfer.
motivation: Simulation is cheap and safe, so challenges like Habitat Challenge 2019 rely on it. If sim rankings do not predict real-robot performance, progress in simulation may be illusory. The authors argue simulators should be judged by sim2real predictivity rather than visual or physical realism.
key_idea: Measure a simulator's predictivity by the Sim2Real Correlation Coefficient (SRCC) between sim and real-robot performance of several navigation models on a virtualized real lab, then tune simulator parameters (sliding off, actuation noise) to maximize SRCC.
insight: Habitat's default collision 'sliding' lets RL agents exploit shortcuts through non-navigable space, which inflates sim success to ~1 while real success varies widely. Disabling sliding raised SRCC_Succ from 0.18 to 0.844 and SRCC_SPL from 0.603 to 0.875, and grid search found zero actuation noise best, suggesting the PyRobot noise model does not match reality. Reconstruction quality also matters: dropping 5% of mesh triangles cut SRCC by 23%.
method: HaPy (Habitat-PyRobot Bridge): a library that treats reality as another simulator; changing config.simulator from Habitat-Sim-v0 to PyRobot-Locobot-v0 runs identical agent, observation, action and metric code on LoCoBot.

Virtualized evaluation: a 6.5m x 10m lab (CODA) with 3 obstacle configurations (easy/medium/hard), 5 waypoints each, scanned with a Matterport Pro2 (~7 panoramas, ~10 min) and imported into Habitat for parallel sim and real trials.

Agent and sim matching: simulated agent radius 0.175m and height 0.61m, 45° FOV, 10m depth clip, PyRobot-derived Gaussian actuation noise; turn angle raised from 10° to 30°; step limit 200 and collision limit 40.
Real localization: a Hokuyo LIDAR with Hector SLAM supplies GPS+Compass and success/SPL (~7cm error vs ~40cm for odometry+IMU).
Navigation models: 9 DD-PPO agents (ResNet50 + 2-layer LSTM, 512-d) with RGB, Depth or RGB→FastDepth predicted depth, trained with different sliding and noise settings.

SRCC: Pearson correlation between sim and real accuracy (SPL or success) over the 9 models, used as an objective for grid search over test-time sim parameters (sliding on/off, noise multiplier 0 to 1).
Wall-following oracle: a top-down-map baseline used to show learned agents are needed in cluttered scenes.

setting.backbone: ResNet50 + 2-layer LSTM policy trained with DD-PPO (9 variants; RGB / Depth / FastDepth-predicted depth)
setting.training_data: 72 Gibson scenes rated 4+ quality, 500M steps on 64 V100s per model, trained from scratch
setting.observation: egocentric RGB or depth (or predicted depth) plus GPS+Compass (LIDAR SLAM in reality) and polar goal
setting.privileged: GPS+Compass localization (Hector SLAM with LIDAR in reality); wall-following oracle uses a top-down map, but only as a baseline

numbers.extra: SRCC over 9 models, 3 room configs x 5 waypoints x 3 trials
numbers.evidence: Fig. 5 and Sec. V-A: 'SRCC_SPL is 0.60'; 'low SRCC_Succ of 0.18'; abstract/intro 0.603

numbers.extra: SRCC over 9 models; simulator parameters tuned on the same real data
numbers.evidence: Fig. 7 / Sec. V-B: 'SRCC_SPL improves from 0.603 to 0.875... SRCC_Succ from 0.18 to 0.844'

numbers.method: Best real model (Depth, train noise 1.0, sliding off)
numbers.extra: real LoCoBot; CODA Test-Sim SPL also given

numbers_note: Not a standard leaderboard benchmark; numbers are sim-vs-real predictivity results on the authors' CODA lab. Real success rates appear only in figures. Table I gives per-model SPL.
results: Under Habitat Challenge 2019 settings SRCC is 0.603 for SPL and 0.18 for success, with 9 rank reversals. Disabling sliding (noise 0) raises these to 0.875 and 0.844 and nearly halves rank reversals to 5 (13.8%). The best real model (Depth, train noise 1.0, sliding off) reaches 0.74 SPL, and the learned agent beats a wall-following oracle on Gibson-val (0.59 vs 0.46 SPL).
limitations: Only 9 models, one lab room with box obstacles, and a single task (PointNav) with LIDAR-SLAM localization, so SRCC estimates are noisy and may not generalize.
Simulation parameters are tuned on the same real-robot data used to measure SRCC, and the best zero actuation noise suggests the noise model itself is poor.
Real testing is costly (40.5 hours) and required larger turn angles and a discrete action space to limit localization noise.
compares_to: Habitat Challenge 2019 simulation settings (sliding on, noise 0)
